idiom_name: explicit ToX / FromX conversion functions in the boundary package (struct tags only for the wire shape)
implementation_notes: Go has no reflection-based mapping culture: the accepted form is a small conversion function per direction - `func ToUserResponse(u domain.User) dto.UserResponse` - plus slice helpers that loop over the scalar mapper, all in one adapter package so neither `domain` nor `dto` imports the other. `encoding/json` struct tags describe the wire names but do not perform domain translation, so the mapper still owns defaults, units and absent values; model those with pointers, `sql.Null*`-style wrappers or explicit sentinel handling rather than zero values. Reflection copiers (mapstructure, copier) exist for mechanical bulk copying of similar structs; prefer explicit functions where compile-time checking and honest defaults matter, and reserve the reflective tools for generic config binding.
pitfalls: Go zero values are silent: a missing JSON field unmarshals to "", 0 or nil, so the mapper cannot tell absent from empty unless the DTO uses pointers or explicit presence flags.
Reflection copiers match by name and skip what does not match; a renamed field or tag then produces half-copied structs with no compile error.
Embedded structs and unexported fields interact badly with both encoding/json and reflection copiers - flatten the DTO deliberately or map field by field.
Returning the DTO type from domain-adjacent packages re-creates the coupling the adapter package exists to prevent.
